question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 7 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 10\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 12\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. 
Given that $D={P}^{T}\,AP,$ where $P$ is an orthogonal matrix, which of the following could be the first and second columns of the matrix $P?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that a matrix $A$ is orthogonally diagonalizable if there exists an orthogonal matrix $P$ such that

$$
A=PD{P}^{T},
$$

where $D$ is a diagonal matrix. Equivalently,

$$
D={P}^{T}AP.
$$

Moreover, a matrix $A$ is orthogonally diagonalizable if and only if it is symmetric.

First, note that $A$ is symmetric and $D$ is diagonal. Therefore, $D={P}^{T}\,AP$ gives an orthogonal diagonalization of $A.$

From the diagonal matrix $D$ we deduce that the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=6,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=6,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=12.$ So, the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2}.$ 

Now, we need to find eigenvectors that correspond to ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=6.$ Computing $A-6I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-6I & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 7 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 10\end{aligned}]-6[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-6I)x=0$ gives two eigenvectors: 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$

Notice that eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are not orthogonal. So, we proceed using the Gram-Schmidt process. We set 

$$
{e}_{1}={v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

and we find ${e}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}_{2} & ={v}_{2}-\frac{{v}_{2}\cdot {e}_{1}}{{e}_{1}\cdot {e}_{1}}{e}_{1} \\  & ={v}_{2}+\frac{2}{5}{e}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+\frac{2}{5}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5} \\ 1 \\ \frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, dividing ${e}_{1}$ and ${e}_{2}$ by their respective norms, we obtain the first and second columns of $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}_{1}}{‖{e}_{1}‖} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5} \\ 0 \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\end{aligned}] \\ \frac{{e}_{2}}{‖{e}_{2}‖} & =\frac{1}{(\frac{\sqrt{30}}{5})}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5} \\ 1 \\ \frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{30}}{30} \\ \frac{\sqrt{30}}{6} \\ \frac{\sqrt{30}}{15}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
